summary: All six acceptance criteria pass on evidence. All five story checks exited 0: web test 505 passed, server/api 343 passed, typecheck, make check, make test (pytest 404 passed). I reviewed the nine in-scope files by reading the diff and sources. Findings are low severity only.

checks.criterion: AC1: /api/v1/openapi.json is OpenAPI 3.1, lists exactly the routed paths and only get operations, with schemas and problem+json errors
checks.evidence: openapi.test.ts:92-106 compares the documented paths with ROUTED_PATHS and with api.routes, and requires every operation method to be 'get'. openapi.test.ts:116-155 checks the 500/4xx problem+json $ref and the 400 on parameterised routes. 343 passed.

checks.criterion: AC2: structural validation with a current OpenAPI 3.1 validator as a devDependency, offline
checks.evidence: apps/web/package.json devDependencies add @seriousme/openapi-schema-validator 2.12.0. openapi.test.ts:77-90 asserts valid:true and version '3.1', and that a document without info.version is refused, so the check is not vacuous. 505 passed.

checks.criterion: AC3: /api/v1/docs serves Scalar HTML with the relative openapi.json URL; any CDN host is declared, not silently allowed
checks.evidence: docs.ts:56-70 uses Scalar({url:'openapi.json', cdn:SCALAR_SCRIPT, ...}) with fonts, telemetry, agent, MCP and developer tools off. docs.test.ts:59-111 checks the relative URL, exactly one pinned script from cdn.jsdelivr.net, no other hosts, and the disabled options. The docs.ts header comment says whether the CSP allows the CDN is a human decision. I did not open the story notes.

checks.criterion: AC4: info carries the API version, read-only and mock-placeholder statements, and no numbers or targets
checks.evidence: openapi.ts:30-48 sets API_VERSION 1.0.0 and the description text. openapi.test.ts:184-212 checks the version, the read-only, GET and HEAD, mock bundle and placeholder wording, and asserts no digit in title, summary or description.

checks.criterion: AC5: Cache-Control is per deploy for both routes
checks.evidence: cache.ts:84-86 deployCacheHeaders; openapi.test.ts:235-260 and docs.test.ts:125-136 assert 'public, max-age=60, immutable', a strong ETag, and 304 on a matching If-None-Match.

checks.criterion: AC6: /api/docs is a permanent redirect to /api/v1/docs, tested, and is the only route outside the base path
checks.evidence: docs.ts:131-137 returns 308 with Location. app.ts:163 mounts it on the root. docs.test.ts:165-172 asserts 308 and Location '/api/v1/docs'. openapi.test.ts:108-114 asserts the redirect is the only route outside /api/v1 and is not in the document.

checks.criterion: Check: pnpm --filter @terraluna/web exec vitest run server/api

checks.evidence: next typegen, tsc --noEmit and tsc -p server/api finished with no errors
ruff, mypy and turbo lint and typecheck all succeeded
pytest 404 passed; turbo web 505 and schema 157 passed

findings.claim: The ETag comment at lines 9-17 still describes only the weak bundle ETag, although contentETag and deployCacheHeaders now add a strong variant.
findings.evidence: The header comment at lines 23-25 covers T15-06, but the earlier paragraph says 'The ETag is weak'. This is a documentation nit with no behaviour impact.

resolution.reason: Fixed in f9db7b2, comments only. The opening paragraph of cache.ts now names both kinds of ETag: the weak bundle ETag (bundleETag) for responses read from the release bundle, and the strong content ETag (contentETag) for /openapi.json and /docs, which only the deploy fixes. The paragraphs that said "The ETag holds the bundle_version" and "The ETag is weak" now say "The bundle ETag", so none of them describes the strong tag as weak. No code changed, and prettier --single-quote --print-width 100 --check passes on the file.

findings.claim: The range diff also touched prd.json and progress.txt, which are outside the story's files list.
findings.evidence: git diff --stat lists scripts/ralph/batches/t15-api/prd.json and progress.txt. They look like Ralph bookkeeping, not product code. I did not read the CSP note for the CDN host there.

resolution.reason: These two paths are the batch's own story list and progress log, which an author iteration is required to edit. The Ralph author instructions say "Change only paths that match the story's files patterns, plus the story list and the progress log", and section 2 says to set review.state to requested, append a progress entry and commit both files as chore(ralph): request review for <id>. In the range 019d7dd..a902948 only that commit touches them (git log -- scripts/ lists a902948 alone). In prd.json it changes only T15-06's own review.state (pending to requested), the review base the loop records, and its notes, where the cdn.jsdelivr.net CSP decision (item 1) sits as AC3 requires. In progress.txt it appends one entry. No product path outside the story's files changed, and ralph.sh's own path check accepted the round.
